extracted.intended_audience: prospective journalism students, applicants, and the general public interested in UC Berkeley Journalism
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of UC Berkeley Graduate School of Journalism's mission, values, faculty role, student attributes, alumni achievements, and areas of study emphasizing practical, platform-based training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: truth-seeking, fact-based, inclusive journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Our mission is to expand the worldwide impact of truth-seeking, fact-based and inclusive journalism by training the next generation of diverse journalists to become exceptional storytellers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames the program's overarching evaluative aim: graduates should practice journalism that is truth-seeking, fact-based, inclusive, and oriented toward broad impact; training focuses on producing 'exceptional storytellers.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty role as thinkers, doers, and mentors
rubrics_metrics.description: Our faculty are both thinkers and doers. They embrace their role as mentors to the next generation of ground-breaking journalists. They teach and inspire, imparting skills and energizing vision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty quality is judged by a combination of intellectual leadership, practical experience, mentorship capacity, and ability to both teach skills and inspire students' vision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired student attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: Our students are Vibrant. Diverse. Curious. Driven. Unafraid. Our students are the future of journalism, compelled by an insatiable desire to investigate and report stories that matter, in any form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students are expected to demonstrate diversity, curiosity, drive, boldness, and a strong investigative impulse; these personal qualities are implicit criteria for fit and success in the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alumni achievement and legacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Our alumni include some of the leading journalists in the world. They produce award-winning and important work — and are paving the way for our current students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program quality is evidenced by alumni accomplishments: leading-journalist status, award-winning work, and ongoing contributions that benefit current students (networking, mentorship, exemplars).

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn-by-doing philosophy / emphasis on student work
rubrics_metrics.description: To understand Berkeley Journalism, look at the work our students are producing. Our philosophy is to learn by doing, and our students are offered many platforms on which to create meaningful journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative emphasis on practical production: students are expected to create real, meaningful journalism across multiple platforms as part of their training; assessment likely values demonstrable work and portfolios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform-specific skill development
rubrics_metrics.description: At Berkeley Journalism, you will learn the essence and craft of journalism that applies to all forms and platforms. Students develop deep skills in particular platforms, working with our faculty to advance skills in audio journalism, documentary, multimedia, narrative writing and photojournalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program criteria include both cross-platform journalistic fundamentals and deep, platform-specific competencies (audio, documentary, multimedia, narrative writing, photojournalism); students are expected to develop mastery in chosen platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional heritage: commitment to free speech
rubrics_metrics.description: Our unique past and vibrant future. On October 1, 1964, Mario Savio climbed onto a police car and ignited the Free Speech Movement, right here in Berkeley.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals an institutional value rooted in Berkeley's Free Speech Movement heritage; implies a normative commitment to free expression and civic engagement as part of the school's identity and evaluative culture.
